hints: The marble enters a cell from one of (up to) three cells in the row above. Do you need anything else about its past to know the best total here?
Row-by-row DP: best[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min of best[r−1][c−1], best[r−1][c], best[r−1][c+1] (only those inside the grid). The answer is the minimum of the last row.

1. prev = copy of the first row.
  2. For each next row r: for each c, cur[c] = grid[r][c] + min of prev[c−1], prev[c], prev[c+1] that exist.
  3. prev = cur.
  4. Return the minimum value in prev.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every starting column and every left/straight/right choice at each row.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Row-by-row DP using only the previous row.

explain: For [[3,1,4],[6,5,2],[7,8,9]]: row 1 becomes [6+1, 5+1, 2+1] = [7,6,3]. Row 2 becomes [7+6, 8+3, 9+3] = [13,11,12]. The minimum is 11 (1 → 2 → 8). Cells can be negative, as in sample 2 (−2 then −6 = −8), so don't start the min with 0 — start it with the straight-down value. Edge columns only have two parents.
recognize: Path from top row to bottom row moving to adjacent columns, minimise sum → row-by-row grid DP over the previous row.
